transform.scale_note: source units are metres: the central table top measures 0.76 m above the levelled floor

colour.method: partial grey-world white balance (strength 0.2) then gamma on sRGB values toward median luminance 0.42 (gamma clamped to [0.75, 1.15])

preview.texture_format: KTX2 ETC1S (basisu -q 255, mipmaps, sRGB), baked on a new UV atlas (xatlas)
preview.simplify: gltfpack -si 0.040000 -se 0.05 on welded positions (from 999999 tris), re-atlased and re-baked

artworks.label: Painted stucco ceiling: Jason and the dragon, the four continents, the Wrangel and von Haugwitz monograms
artworks.location: ceiling
artworks.artist: Hans Zauch (stucco); painting attributed to Nils Eriksson in the museum's photo record
artworks.note: The museum's photo record (LSH photo 30913, republished by the museum on Wikimedia Commons) states the stucco ceiling was made by Hans Zauch in 1663-1664; LSH photo 88015 names Nils Eriksson for the painted stucco. Zauch died 1666 (https://www.wikidata.org/wiki/Q30331456).

artworks.label: Carved and painted fireplace (Markus Hebel) and relief-tiled stove
artworks.location: east wall (+x)
artworks.note: The same museum record: wooden fireplace with sculptures by Markus Hebel (1663), screens decorated by Johan Malchow, and a stove with reliefs by Hindrich Thim (1670). Hebel died 1664 (https://www.wikidata.org/wiki/Q27300028).

artworks.label: Room fabric: gilt-leather wall hangings (SKO 633), painted joinery, limestone floor
artworks.location: walls and floor
artworks.note: The gilt leather is catalogued 1650-1700; the castle was built 1654-1676 (https://skoklostersslott.se/skoklosters-slotts-historia/).
